subject: Materials Science
title: Tempered Glass: Shatter-Safe
description: Learn Tempered Glass: Shatter-Safe in one minute.

hook.text: A car side window explodes into tiny cubes when broken — no sharp daggers, by design.

buildup.text: Tempered glass is heated to 620°C then rapidly cooled by air jets on both surfaces.

discovery.text: The surface freezes first and goes into compression, while the core remains in tension.

twist.text: That compressive skin makes it four times stronger — but once cracked, all tension releases at once.

climax.text: The explosive shattering into small cubes is actually a safety feature — no lethal shards.

punchline.text: Tempered glass is built to break safely.

quiz.question: Why does tempered glass shatter into small cubes?
options: It is made from a different type of glass
Built-in tension releases all at once when cracked
A special coating causes it to crumble
